claims.text: MIP figures were first disclosed publicly alongside NIP totals for FY2010; the Department publishes only an aggregate topline and states that other MIP budget details remain classified.

The NIP/MIP division creates a jurisdictional seam between the intelligence committees and the armed services committees that a single activity scored across both can be described to each committee without either receiving a complete account. Reasoning: the two programmes have different controlling officials (DNI and SECDEF) and different primary oversight committees, and no statute requires a reconciled cross-programme presentation to any single body.

connections.note: The Military Intelligence Program is the defence-side counterpart to the NIP, managed by the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security. DoD has disclosed a MIP appropriated topline annually since 2010 and request figures since 2012; the DoD Financial Management Regulation Vol. 2B Ch. 16 governs how intelligence programmes are budgeted and displayed. Topline-only disclosure is the same structural property as the NIP.

connections.label: National Intelligence Program (NIP)
connections.note: The NIP is controlled by the Director of National Intelligence and the MIP by the Secretary of Defense; both are published only as annual aggregates. Attested by ODNI's own budget page and the FAS compilation.

sources.name: ODNI, IC Budget; FAS Intelligence Budget Data

desc: The Military Intelligence Program was created in 2005 by consolidating the Joint Military Intelligence Program and the Tactical Intelligence and Related Activities aggregation, placing under the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence (now Intelligence and Security) the intelligence money that supports military operations, as distinct from the National Intelligence Program controlled by the DNI. The Department of Defense publishes only an aggregate topline for the MIP, in a brief annual press release, with the standing formula that no other MIP budget figures or details will be released because they remain classified. Appropriated toplines have run from $20.0 billion in FY2007 to a peak of $29.8 billion in FY2024 and $27.8 billion in FY2025, against a FY2026 request of $33.6 billion - roughly a third of the NIP in each year. The MIP matters to this board more than the NIP does, because it is the pot of money closest to the Department's own laboratories, test ranges, materiel commands and special access program enterprise, and because its governing official, USD(I&S), is also the Department's Senior Security Official with authority over the SAP system. The NIP and MIP split also creates the oversight seam that any concealed activity would exploit: NIP money is overseen by the intelligence committees, MIP money principally by the armed services committees, and a programme scored partly to each can be described truthfully to each committee in terms that leave neither with the whole.
